title: What Questions Should I Ask Before Hiring an Architect in Westchester NY
excerpt: Hiring the right architect for your Westchester home project matters. Here are the key questions that separate good matches from poor fits.
content:
You're thinking about renovating your kitchen, adding a second story, or maybe building something from scratch. Before you hire someone, you need to know who you're actually working with. The right questions now save headaches later.

Picking a licensed architect in Westchester NY isn't just about checking a box. It's about finding someone who understands your home, your neighborhood, and how to actually get the job done without getting stuck in the permitting process.

Are They Licensed and Can They Actually Build?

Start here. Ask if your architect holds a current New York State architecture license. That matters. But here's the thing: some architects can design beautiful spaces and then hand the project off to someone else to build. That creates gaps.

Find out if they're also a licensed general contractor. When one person holds both licenses, they understand the full picture. Design decisions don't happen in a vacuum away from construction reality. A licensed architect in New York who also runs jobs as a contractor knows exactly what works and what doesn't before the first nail gets driven.

Who Actually Runs Your Project?

Ask who will oversee your job from start to finish. Will you work with the principal, or get handed off to someone else halfway through? This matters more than you'd think, especially on bigger projects like a primary suite addition in Scarsdale or a historic restoration in Tarrytown.

When you hire someone to design your renovation in Westchester, you want the same person managing it through completion. Continuity matters. Your architect should be there for all the decisions, not just the pretty drawings.

What's Their Experience With Your Town's Permitting?

Every municipality in Westchester County has its own building department and permit process. White Plains works differently than Bronxville. Rye has its own rules. Larchmont has theirs. This is normal and standard across the county.

A residential architect in Scarsdale or someone doing home additions in Westchester should know the local process cold. Ask which towns they've worked in recently. Ask about their average approval timeline. Ask what common hold-ups they've seen and how they handle them.

You want someone who's done this dance before. Not someone learning your building department on your dime.

Do They Manage the Whole Project or Just Design?

Some architects hand you drawings. Others oversee construction start to finish. Ask what's included. Will they visit the site regularly? Will they handle change orders? Who's the point person if something doesn't match the plans?

A design-build approach in Westchester means one firm handles both the architecture and the construction management. When you hire that way, accountability stays clear. You're not caught between an architect and a contractor pointing fingers.

What's Their Real Track Record?

Ask for references. Not just names, but people who've done similar work. If you want a custom home in Westchester County, talk to someone who's built one. If you need a kitchen remodel, ask about their last three.

Go look at finished work if you can. Ask about projects that hit snags and how they were handled. Real experience shows up in the details.
